# Payload conformance fixtures (canonical)

`payloads.json` in this directory is the **canonical shared fixture set** for
the stash share-payload codec (v6 wire format). It was promoted from the
`spikes/codec-conformance` corpus (F3), which originally copied it from the
e2e fixtures; the e2e copy (`packages/e2e/fixtures/payloads.json`) is
generated by [`generate.ts`](./generate.ts) and must stay byte-compatible
with this file (drift is caught by the Go conformance test, which fails if
the count is not 13).

## Consumers (read-only; do not edit vectors here to satisfy a test)

- Go: `daemon/internal/codec/codec_test.go` (conformance, both directions)
- Go: `daemon/internal/mcpserver/decode_fixture_test.go` (`stash_decode` integration)
- TS: `packages/codec/src/__tests__/conformance.test.ts`
- F11 conformance target and F12 `/s/#p=` route tests (planned)
- `packages/evals`, `packages/server-core` (existing loaders via `@stash/shared/fixtures`)

## Schema

Top level: array of fixtures.

| field        | type             | notes |
|--------------|------------------|-------|
| `name`       | string           | stable id, referenced by tests and e2e steps |
| `description`| string           | human context |
| `fragment`   | string           | the full `#p=` / `#q=` URL fragment. Decode target. |
| `itemCount`  | number           | decoded item count |
| `items`      | `{url,title}[]`  | decoded items in order |
| `title`      | string?          | optional stash title (`t`) |
| `tags`       | string[]?        | optional tags (`g`) |
| `note`       | string?          | optional note (`n`) |

Wire format: prefix `C`/`R` = base64url (`#p=`), `D`/`S` = base32 (`#q=`),
where `C`/`D` are brotli-compressed msgpack and `R`/`S` raw msgpack; all
fragments are v6. Encoders emit **no** base64/base32 padding, but decoders
tolerate stripped/partial padding (`@oslojs` ignore-padding on the TS side,
padding-trimmed strict decode in Go).

## Known fixture quirks

- **five-tabs odd length.** The five-tabs base64url body is 213 characters
  (odd), which is not a valid unpadded base64url length for the byte count it
  must encode. It is a generation artifact from an earlier brotli-wasm
  output that tolerated trailing partial-symbol handling; both decoders
  accept it via padding/last-symbol tolerance, so the vector is kept as-is.
  Go handles it by trimming `=` padding and using the stdlib unpadded
  decoder, which accepts the dangling partial symbol exactly like
  `decodeBase64urlIgnorePadding`.
- **empty-items.** The fragment is empty (`#p=`) and both implementations
  refuse it with `Invalid URL fragment format` (parity by refusal); it is
  asserted as an error case, never decoded.
- **Expiry.** All non-expired fixtures share one generation timestamp
  (`expiry = 1787567265`); `expired` carries `1787477265`. Tests use a fixed
  clock between the two.

## Assertion invariant

**Bidirectional semantic round-trip, never byte-identical.** Go decode of a
TS-authored fragment must equal the expected items/metadata, and TS decode of
a Go-encoded payload must match too. Compressed bytes differ between
`brotli-wasm` (TS) and `andybalholm/brotli` (Go); nothing downstream may
assert byte equality. See `spikes/codec-conformance` history (now removed)
and the local-first replatform spec Appendix B for the measurements behind
this rule.
